question: How does the Lord's all-gracious power include even those deemed unfit for Vedic rites?
premises: Fix the mind on the Lord, become His devotee and worshipper, bow to Him, and come to Him alone.
Sinful wombs, animals, birds, reptiles, women, vaiśyas, śūdras, and dependent persons who take refuge in the Lord worship Him alone.
The supremely compassionate Lord's deeds, such as Gajendra's liberation, are heard in thousands.
Some read the verse as praise of twice-born and kṣatriyas rather than as intent of liberation for women and others.
Such readers fragment the Lord's all-gracious power and cannot endure His supreme compassion.
The Lord has no enemy and no dear one, even one of evil conduct.
Other clear-meaning statements are contradicted by those who force difference into the nondual Lord-essence and ignore scriptural contradictions.
When questioned, those obsessed with caste, envy, shame, and crooked gaze impute comic rasa to people's false prattle.
inference: The verse affirms that the Lord's grace is universally accessible and rejects restrictive, caste-based readings as distortions of nondual compassion.
uncertainties: Several fused compounds are difficult to parse with certainty.
The exact scope of 'some' and their intended opponents is not fully clear.
Some tokens appear corrupt or abbreviated, so precise syntactic relations remain uncertain.
plain_english: Fix your mind on me, become my devotee and worshipper, bow to me, and you will come to me alone. Even those born in sinful wombs, animals, birds, reptiles, women, vaiśyas, śūdras, and dependent persons who take refuge in me worship me alone. The supremely compassionate Lord's deeds, such as the liberation of the elephant king, are heard in thousands. Some interpret the verse as praise of twice-born and kṣatriyas, not as an intent of liberation for women and others; they fragment the Lord's all-gracious power and cannot endure His supreme compassion. The Lord has no enemy and no dear one, even one of evil conduct. Other clear statements are contradicted by those who forcibly introduce difference into the nondual essence of the Lord and ignore scriptural contradictions. When questioned, those deeply immersed in caste obsession, envy, shame, and crooked gaze impute comic rasa to the false prattle of all people. The commentary makes all auspicious.
